creator.name: Unknown painters of the Barrier Canyon style

object.description: A line of tall, armless, hollow-eyed figures painted in dark red along sixty metres of a sandstone alcove in Horseshoe Canyon, Utah. The Great Gallery is the finest panel of the Barrier Canyon style, named after this canyon; its largest figure, the Holy Ghost, stands over two metres tall and was painted by spraying pigment, with smaller animals and figures around it.
facts: Geologists dated the panel in 2014 by the age of the rockfall it was painted on and the sediment that later buried its base: between about 1 and 1100 CE.
The full panel is about 61 metres long and 4.6 metres high.
Horseshoe Canyon was renamed from Barrier Canyon, but the style kept the old name.
